expected_evidence: Geological: abrupt freshwater-signature excursions in North Atlantic marine sediment cores (planktonic foraminiferal δ18O shifts, ice-rafted debris pulses) consistent with a meltwater discharge (e.g., via the St. Lawrence or Mackenzie/Arctic outflow) coinciding with YD onset ~12.9 ka
Geological: AMOC-proxy weakening signals (Pa/Th ratios, benthic-planktonic δ13C gradients) in North Atlantic cores dated to the YD onset

Ice-core evidence (Greenland GISP2/NGRIP/GRIP): abrupt δ18O cooling step, dust and sea-salt spikes, and ammonium/biomass-burning proxies (elevated NH4+, black carbon, ammonium spikes) at the YD onset layer
Geological/sedimentary: continent-wide charcoal and soot layers in lake and bog sediments indicating a widespread biomass-burning event at the YD boundary

Geological: putative YD boundary-layer markers sometimes cited for an 'impact winter' mechanism (magnetic spherules, nanodiamonds, platinum anomaly, black mat) at multiple sites — contested in the literature (model-prior: this evidence set is specifically associated with the competing Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis, not the meltwater-forcing mechanism, so its presence under this hypothesis's stated mechanism is internally inconsistent)
Material/archaeological: disruption or reorganization of Clovis-era North American lithic traditions and site-occupation patterns around 12.9–12.8 ka, changes in megafaunal bone assemblages
Genetic: population bottleneck or turnover signatures in North American megafauna and human (Paleoindian) ancient DNA around the YD transition

Astronomical: absence or presence of an impact crater/extraterrestrial fallout signature dated to ~12.9 ka (relevant mainly to the biomass-burning-impact-winter mechanism, less so to a meltwater-pulse actor)

Model-prior: broader literature debate (Broecker's freshwater/AMOC-shutdown hypothesis vs. Firestone et al.-style cosmic impact hypothesis) as background context, not derived from the provided evidence text
response.rationale: The stated interval (-11000 to -10001) falls squarely within the Younger Dryas period bucket, so the 'younger-dryas' detectability row is the correct reference (geological 0.65, material 0.35, genetic 0.30, astronomical 0.70, textual 0.0, others low). The Younger Dryas onset is one of the best-preserved and most intensively studied abrupt climate transitions in the Quaternary record: Greenland ice cores, varved lake sediments, marine sediment cores, and speleothems provide high-resolution, well-dated archives that plausibly capture both a meltwater/AMOC-weakening signal and any biomass-burning proxy (ammonium, charcoal, soot) at the relevant time horizon. This makes non-detection harder to excuse on preservation grounds alone for geological and, to a lesser extent, material evidence — absence of such signals would be more informative of falsity than of poor survivability, unlike genetic, linguistic, oral_tradition, or textual channels, which are essentially uninformative this far back (textual=0, linguistic=0.05, oral_tradition=0.1) and where absence carries little weight against the hypothesis. One important caveat (flagged as model-prior, not drawn from the supplied evidence text): the hypothesis's specific pairing of a 'meltwater-pulse' actor with a 'biomass-burning-impact-winter' mechanism is mechanistically unusual — mainstream freshwater-forcing accounts explain YD cooling via AMOC/ocean-circulation shutdown, whereas biomass-burning/'impact winter' signatures (nanodiamonds, platinum anomaly, spherules, black mat) are specifically associated with the rival Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis. This internal mismatch means that even if biomass-burning proxies are found in the geological record (which they plausibly could be, given good preservation), they would not straightforwardly corroborate a meltwater-pulse-as-trigger mechanism, so evidentiary support for this exact causal chain is weaker than the raw detectability scores suggest. I nudge the effective adjustment down slightly from the raw geological/astronomical ceiling (0.65–0.70) to ~0.55 to reflect that even well-preserved evidence may not cleanly discriminate between competing YD-onset mechanisms, while still keeping it well above genetic/textual/linguistic channels which are largely uninformative for this period.
